header: Pure helpers for the omni search page. I keep them free of DB, network and React.

1. decideLoginHint(): decides when the page should SUGGEST signing in / asking for a written summary. I suggest it only for an explanatory question ("why ...", "explain ...", "policy on ...") that was answered with plain circular cards. Executive Deep Synthesis gives a written summary with sources for questions that compare or trace circulars; there is no button (step 41a): the Enter key sends such a question from a signed-in executive there by itself. So a signed-out visitor is told to sign in first if they are an executive, and a signed-in executive whose question was NOT sent there is told how to ask for a summary. I suggest nothing for names, counts, holiday dates, quoted exact phrases, or when the synthesis was already used. I deliberately do NOT handle masked mobile numbers / email IDs here: clicking a masked value already opens the login page. This is a rule of thumb.

2. excludeShownPeople(): the page prints people from two independent searches (the answer card and the directory name search). I make sure a person already shown in the first list is not printed again in the second.

doc: The page also has a "title" mode, so I keep this a plain string. Only "intellectual" matters here.

members.name: authStatus
doc: The state of the session. I give the EDS sign-in advice only to a visitor who is DEFINITELY signed out ("unauthenticated"), never while the session is still being checked ("loading"). When it is not passed, it is derived from `authenticated`.

members.name: edsEnabled
doc: The kill switch of the automatic EDS route (autoEdsEnabled). When EDS is switched off, I tell nobody to sign in for it. Default: on.

members.name: executiveAskAnsweredNo
doc: The visitor was ASKED "Are you an executive?" for this very question and answered No. The simple answer is then what was asked for, so I do not repeat the sign-in advice above it.

doc: The advice given to a SIGNED-OUT visitor whose question belongs to Executive Deep Synthesis. I let ONE detector decide which questions those are, the same one that routes a signed-in executive's question (synthesisIntent.ts: level "synthesis", never the weaker "borderline"), so the advice and the route can never disagree.

symbols.name: looksAnalytical
doc: I call a question analytical when it is explanatory, as opposed to a lookup (name, count, date, id).

symbols.name: PEOPLE_NOUN
doc: These are the shapes the plain search answers directly from the records (employee counts and lists, seniority, contact lookups, a ticket number, a holiday with a year). I keep this deliberately NARROW: when unsure, say nothing, because a wrong "use plain search" tip on a circular question is worse than no tip.

doc: I drop from `others` anyone whose ticket number is already present in `shown`. Rows with no ticket are kept. After the "sign in" advice: the visitor signs in as an executive WHILE the EDS question is still on the screen. I want the question to then run by itself through EDS (what the Enter key would have done for an executive), not stay as the plain circular answer the signed-out visit got. True only for a visit that went from not-an-executive to executive, with the window open, the answer on screen being the plain search (not EDS already) of a question that cleanly falls in the EDS group (same detector as the advice), and the box still holding that question (not edited since).

symbols.name: ExecutiveAsk
doc: THE QUESTION "ARE YOU AN EXECUTIVE?" (my decision, 17 Nov 2026). When a line is clearly an EDS-category question (the same detector that routes an executive's question: level "synthesis") and the visitor is DEFINITELY signed out, nothing is searched yet: the bar first asks whether he is an executive. Yes -> he is told that EDS replies come to executives who are signed in, and offered the Sign in button; when he has signed in as an executive with the same question still in the box, it runs by itself through EDS. No -> the simple reply (the normal search) is shown, as for any other question, and the sign-in advice is not repeated. While the session is still being checked ("loading"), and for a signed-in person (an executive goes to EDS, anyone else to the normal search), I ask nothing.

members.name: said
doc: "yes" means he said he is an executive and was told to sign in; null means not answered yet
